newsitem.title: USA: SoCal Ed seeks alliance with Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: SoCal Ed seeks alliance with Los Angeles.

text.p: Southern California Edison said Tuesday it will ask City of Los Angeles Board of Water & Power Commissioners to consider a strategic alliance between the utilities.
This would position the city's Department of Water and Power for market competition, beginning next year, the Edison International subsidiary explained.
The board will meet at 1000 PST/1300 EST/1800 GMT at the department's downtown headquarters to consider staff recommendations for a strategic partner for the nation's largest municipal utility.

Over the past nine months, SoCal Edison said, proposals of three out-of-state energy firms to provide the city utility with marketing and asset management expertise have surfaced as finalists in a solicitation and review process that excluded Edison and other large California utilities.
Last week, the city named the three as PacifiCorp, Enron Corp, and a partnership of Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus.
In a presentation to the Commissioners, SoCal Edison President Stephen E. Frank will appeal to the Board to include Edison in the process, the company said.
Frank will outline the added value and advantages of an alliance with the nation's second largest investor-owned electric utility whose service territory borders DWP's Los Angeles service area.
This proposal represents potential value estimated at $100 million a year, or $1 billion over 10 years, the utility said.

"We hope the DWP commissioners will see the clear advantages and opportunities available to them only through an Edison/DWP alliance," Frank said. "Both utilities share a unique alignment of interests."

He said both utilities "must reduce costs, provide new products and services to customers and position ourselves for the emerging competitive era. Our aligned interests, geographical proximity and commitment to the local economy provide a unique opportunity for a broad-based strategic alliance to benefit both companies and their customers."
Frank will outline a general alliance strategy that can enable DWP to reduce costs, increase revenues, offer new products, reduce debt and provide reliable service.

"We would bring our skills, systems, standards, infrastructure, technologies, reliability management, wholesale trading and new retail products to DWP customers through such an alliance," Frank said. "Our proposal does not seek a buyout or merger with DWP."

The DWP invited proposals only from energy firms with power generating capacity of less than 7,000 megawats, which automatically excluded Rosemead-based SoCal Edison and San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co -- California's two largest utilities.
